selected_primary_idea.title: Clinical Delegation Boundary Contract (CDBC)
selected_primary_idea.summary: A task-level authorization contract that ties AI outputs to intended use, uncertainty-aware abstention, clinician escalation, equity audit, accountable review, monitoring, and revocation rules.
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: screening-mammography case x site x patient subgroup x model state x uncertainty x delegation tier x clinician action x outcome
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: A CDBC-guided pathway will provide a better safety-adjusted delegation profile than AI-only or unspecified human-AI workflows, even when the underlying prediction model is unchanged.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: The contract places every output into a named authority tier and requires escalation when uncertainty, data completeness, distribution, equity, or lifecycle gates fail.
falsifiers: CDBC gates add no early detection of unsafe or inequitable conditions
human escalation does not improve the safety-adjusted endpoint
an independent auditor cannot reconstruct a delegation decision
workflow burden outweighs measured patient- or service-relevant benefit

competitive_ideas.title: Higher-AUC model search
competitive_ideas.reason: Technically useful but incomplete for authority, accountability, and care-episode safety.

high_risk_ideas.title: Fully autonomous screening decision
high_risk_ideas.reason: Requires stronger task-specific evidence, regulation, and accountable governance than is currently established.

rejected_ideas.reason: No stable clinical task, reference standard, harm model, or delegation boundary.
Overgeneralizes against evidence of task-specific automation potential.

mcts_evolution.change: add subgroup gates and pause trigger
define authority, overrides, workload, and response timing
add monitoring, incident review, and revocation
